regions.region: page 1 title, authors, abstract, graphical abstract, keywords, and introduction
regions.finding: Verified the source-derived title and the aggregate claim of five asymmetric Ru-catalyzed C–H activation classes. The graphical abstract and introductory structures summarize the strategy and applications; they do not provide independent row conditions or yields.

regions.region: page 1 introduction and prior-work discussion
regions.finding: The cited Yu, Albicker/Cramer, Ackermann, and other prior chiral-directing-group work is contextual literature. It was not expanded into experiments of the current article.

unresolved: No experiment-specific arrow occurs on page 1.
The online Supporting Information statement does not establish a workspace SI association.

regions.region: page 2 upper Scheme 1 and surrounding strategy discussion
regions.finding: Scheme 1 is a generic current-paper overview of reactions A–E and synthetic applications; it is classified as a general scheme rather than a single experiment.

regions.region: page 2 lower Scheme 2 reaction header, 3a–3w product grid, and footnotes
regions.finding: Twenty-three distinct Reaction A scope rows were retained with shared charges, N2, THF, 55 °C/12 h, row yields or trace, and ee where reported. The parenthesized 3b result plus footnote b is a separate 3.0 mmol-scale repeat. Footnote a is configuration provenance for 3a.

regions.region: page 2 lower-right scope prose and 1-hexene limitation
regions.finding: The prose restates scope trends without creating duplicate rows. The source reports an unsuccessful reaction of ‘3a’ with 1-hexene; that exact potentially inconsistent label and the failure are preserved in an unresolved record.

unresolved: The 1-hexene statement calls the reacting material 3a, which may be a source-label inconsistency; it was not silently corrected.
The gram-scale footnote does not restate scaled charges for all other components.

regions.region: page 3 upper-left Scheme 3 Reaction B
regions.finding: All four 5a–5d scope products were retained as independent experiments with shared charges, N2, 50 °C/72 h, yields, and ee. CCDC 2313647 for 5c is characterization only.

regions.region: page 3 upper-right Scheme 4 Reaction C and limitations
regions.finding: All six 7a–7f scope products were retained separately at 55 °C/36 h with >20:1 dr. The parenthesized 18% 7a result under Reaction A conditions is a separate control. Two benzonorbornadiene failures are separate unresolved records; CCDC 2305481 for 7e is characterization only.

regions.region: page 3 lower Scheme 5 applications a–d
regions.finding: Eight arrows were represented as eight experiments: reduction of 3m, formation and demethylation of 3x, reduction of 7b, preparation of 6c, standard-condition formation of 7g, reduction to 12, and Rh-mediated conversion to 13. The 0 °C-to-room-temperature demethylation was split into ordered stages with missing ramp time.

regions.region: page 3 bottom Scheme 6 beginning
regions.finding: The A–C pathway is a proposed mechanism; I–IV are not isolated preparations and no mechanistic branch was assigned a synthetic yield.

unresolved: Most Scheme 3–5 arrows omit workups, purification, isolated masses, and outcome measurement bases.
Several Scheme 5 arrows omit reaction times; those times remain null/missing.

regions.region: page 4 upper Scheme 6 continuation and byproduct discussion
regions.finding: The text completes the proposed A–C mechanism and rationalizes amine 14 capture or decomposition to 15–17. These are mechanistic/byproduct entities, not independent reaction runs.

regions.region: page 4 middle-left Reaction D optimization prose
regions.finding: The prose gives the path to optimized Ru/AgPF6/Zn(OAc)2 conditions and refers optimization rows to SI Table S4. Because SI is not associated, no unseen optimization rows were inferred.

regions.region: page 4 lower Scheme 7 reaction header, 19a–19s grid, and footnotes
regions.finding: Nineteen scope rows were retained independently with shared charges, N2, THF, 48 h, row temperatures, yields or trace, and ee where reported. Footnote a is configuration provenance. Footnote b states 2.5 mmol amide but its product-row marker is not legible, so the quantity is preserved in an unassigned unresolved record rather than attached to a row.

regions.region: page 4 lower-right scope prose
regions.finding: The ortho-methyl benzamide is explicitly unreactive with 4-nitrobenzaldehyde and is retained as a failed Reaction D scope record; narrative summaries were not duplicated.

unresolved: The row governed by Scheme 7 footnote b could not be determined from the original image.
Reaction D optimization details assigned to unassociated SI Table S4 remain unavailable.

regions.region: page 5 upper-left Scheme 8 scale-up and recovery
regions.finding: The 2.5 mmol Reaction D scale-up retains separate 19b and oxazolidine-20 outcomes. Hydrolysis of 20 followed by Boc capture is one two-stage sequence, and the 82% value remains a two-step yield to 21 rather than a second-stage yield.

regions.region: page 5 upper-right Scheme 9 application discussion
regions.finding: The prose introduces the natural-product and pharmaceutical applications whose visible arrows and outcomes occur on page 6. It is linked to those records without creating summary duplicates.

regions.region: page 5 lower-left control-experiment discussion for Scheme 10a–e
regions.finding: Nine distinct mechanistic controls were retained: two isolated ruthenacycle formations, one staged in-situ Ru-A/18b run, one Ru-A catalyst replacement, two 50 mol% scrambling tests, and three chiral-matching rows. Only page-5 textual facts were imported; page-7-only image details were not used.

regions.region: page 5 lower-right beginning of Scheme 11 mechanism discussion
regions.finding: The Ru-A/Ru-A′ Reaction D cycle is a proposed mechanism. Intermediates are not isolated preparations, and continuation facts beyond page 6 were not claimed.

unresolved: Several control temperatures, quantities, and times are absent from page-5 text and were not imported from the unregistered page-7 context image.
Scheme 11 continues outside the covered page range.

regions.region: page 6 full-page Scheme 9 panels a–f
regions.finding: Every visible reaction arrow was classified: eight Reaction D application runs, four BBr3 demethylations, the 19ae/19ae′ mixture run plus separate crystallization, one unresolved four-step preparation of 1x, and two reference-marked literature conversions. Standard-condition arrows inherit Reaction D quantities only where explicitly invoked; Zn(OPiv)2 and temperature overrides are retained.

regions.region: page 6 Scheme 9b and 9d selectivity annotations
regions.finding: The 38% value remains the total yield of the 19ae/19ae′ mixture with 5:1 ratio and 89% ee for the major isomer; the subsequent single crystallization has its own 75% and >99% ee outcomes. The 19aa-to-19ab 0 °C-to-room-temperature arrow is split into addition, warming, and hold stages with missing times.

regions.region: page 6 Scheme 9 literature/reference arrows
regions.finding: 19ab-to-19ac (Ref. 34) and the two-step 19ag-to-19ah conversion are classified as literature examples, not current-paper experiments. No missing literature procedures or yields were invented.

unresolved: Most Scheme 9 derivatization arrows omit scale, reagent dose, time, workup, purification, mass, and yield basis.
The four steps from 3-methoxybenzaldehyde to 1x are not specified on this page.
Complex structures remain source-labeled and machine-unverified.
